title: Building Treehouses
lead: How can you make a welcoming treehouse where everyone wants to come play?
notes: Purpose
Children build a treehouse with blocks, cardboard, and parts of trees.
This is a two-part learning experience that continues in Week 4.
Big Ideas
Color is a property of many natural and human-made things.
We can all communicate about colors.
Guiding Questions
How can we explore and communicate ideas and feelings through colors?
How do colors provide information?
Family Engagement
Invite families to share their childhood experiences with treehouses.
Vocabulary
treehouse: a structure built within the branches of a tree, usually for children to play in
sign: information - words or pictures - hung up for people to read or see
directions: how to get somewhere
collaborate: to work with someone else on something
Materials and Preparation
Strictly No Elephants, Lisa Mantchev Flag page 24
wooden unit blocks
colored blocks
sticks, branches, wood cuttings (that have been sanded)
cardboard
Treehouse Visuals
Simple Block Structures: Treehouses
Hang the Treehouse Visuals and Simple Block Structures: Treehouses in the Block Center. Bring a few blocks and the Strictly No Elephants book to Intro to Centers.
Intro to Centers
In Strictly No Elephants, the children turn a treehouse into a place for all to play - people of all skin colors, languages, and abilities.
Point to the treehouse on page 24.

The children make signs - papers with words on them - for their treehouse to show that everyone is welcome, and one friend stands nearby to help give people directions for how to get to the treehouse.
Point to the signs and the child giving directions in the illustration.
This week in the Block Center, you can collaborate - work together - to build a treehouse using blocks. How can you make a welcoming treehouse where everyone wants to come play?
During Centers

Encourage children to reference the Treehouse Visuals for visuals, and then to make a plan or design together before building. Invite children to think about what makes a space feel welcoming to them, and how they can incorporate that into their designs.

Support children in building more complex structures by modeling stacking blocks on top of each other. Provide rich vocabulary about their structures that support their building, such as “stable” and “symmetrical.”
Differentiation Ideas
Children can work with smaller blocks at a table or other surface if maneuvering unit blocks is a challenge.
Children could create the perimeter of the tree house using unit blocks or cardboard blocks and play inside of it.
Children (or children in collaboration with adults) can make signs for the block area for other children to use, or can make a map or directions for how to get to the treehouse.
If a child would benefit from more specific play guidance, reference the Simple Block Structures visuals to help them get started.
For further modified learning experiences, see: Blocks, Building Autumn Trees and Treehouses Differentiated Access.
Facilitation
What color do you want to make your treehouse?
How can you make everyone feel welcome in your treehouse?
What sign can you make for the treehouse? How would that sign be helpful?
Extensions
Children can draw their treehouse design after building it to help them share their ideas and build representational drawing skills.
Create a treehouse inside, on the playground, or in an outdoor classroom.
Try building with different kinds of materials.
Standards
PreK.SEL8 The child will engage socially, and build relationships with other children and with adults.
PreK.APL4 The child will demonstrate creativity in thinking and use of materials.
PreK.APL5 The child will cooperate with others in play and learning.

title: Color Party Invitations
lead: Who should come to our Color Party? Have the teacher-completed invitations ready, then decorate the borders.
notes: Purpose
Children decorate invitations to let their families and friends know about a Color Party that will mark the end of the unit.
Vocabulary
invitation: a note that tells where and when to come to special event
Materials and Preparation
invitations to the Color Party Complete the invitations. Then copy and cut in half for children to decorate the border.
colored pencils or crayons, to decorate invitations
classroom calendar
clipboard or whiteboard and markers

Plan a date for your Color Party, a classroom celebration to mark the end of the unit, near the end of Week 6. Consult with families and caregivers about a time when they are most likely to be able to attend. If the families you work with are unlikely to be able to join during school hours, consider an evening or weekend event. You could also plan to invite other classes or members of the school community to your party.
Intro to Centers
We are learning so much about colors in our classroom. In a few weeks, we will have a color party to share our learning with our families and friends.
If you have a calendar in the classroom, demonstrate adding a note to the calendar that says “color party” on the day the party is scheduled.
Who should come to our party?
Write down children’s ideas on clipboard or whiteboard.
What should we do during the party? What should we wear? What colorful food should we serve?
Continue to write down children’s ideas.
We need to let our families and friends know that they should come to the party. We need to make invitations - or notes that tell where and when to come to a special event.
During Centers
Support children to decorate the invitations and write or dictate the names of family and friends if they choose. Children may also choose to draw a picture of the person they want to invite.
After Centers

Send the invitations home to families at the end of the week, so that families can plan ahead to attend the Color Party in Week 6. Be sure to send a reminder to families as well, closer to the date of your party.
Standards
W.PK.2 Use a combination of dictating and drawing to supply information about a topic.
Invitation template
Come to our Color Party!

Please come to our classroom to see what we have learned during our World of Color unit. We can’t wait to show you our artwork, share the book we have made, and show what we have been learning through play! Remember to wear your favorite color!
Teacher preparation clarification
The source template is two identical invitations on one page, separated by a cutting line. Teacher completes Date and Time before copying; children decorate the borders.

The source names the setting only as “our classroom.” No calendar date, time, named school/classroom location, or family/friend names were supplied. Do not invent them. Teacher confirms arrangements and supplies the actual details; children may choose whom to invite.

The displayed supplemental illustration is an invitation-decorating cue, not the original printable template or a photograph of this class. Use the linked source template, with the actual teacher-confirmed Date and Time filled in, before children decorate the borders. No child or family information is collected by this lesson.
